You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testEqualsCS2()` from `StringUtilsTest` tests the `StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence)` method. This method compares two character sequences for equality. 

Inspecting the `StringUtils.equals` method, it calls `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches` with the parameters:
- cs1
- ignoreCase=false
- start indices 0, 0
- length = Math.max(cs1.length(), cs2.length())

Inside `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches`, the code attempts to compare characters in the two sequences starting from the given indices for the given length. The key issue is that the length passed to `regionMatches` is the maximum of the lengths of the two sequences. However, when `regionMatches` tries to iterate through the characters via `charAt(index1++)` and `charAt(index2++)`, if one sequence is shorter than this length, an index out of bounds error will occur.

This explains the current bug report that the method can fail with String Index Out Of Bounds Exception if the two sequences are of different lengths. The test `testEqualsCS2()` triggers this by calling `StringUtils.equals(new StringBuilder("abc"), "abcd")`, where the second sequence is longer, leading to an OOB exception in `regionMatches`.

The fix should be to use the minimum length of the two sequences when calling `regionMatches` in `StringUtils.equals` so that no character access goes beyond the length of any sequence.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this specific issue.

Hence, the bug occurs due to using the maximum length instead of the minimum length when comparing the two sequences character by character in `StringUtils.equals`. This leads to accessing characters beyond the end of the shorter sequence in `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches`.

Recommended fix location is the method:
- `StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence)`
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testEqualsCS2()` exercises the method `StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence)`. The implementation of this method calls `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches` with the length argument set to the maximum of the lengths of the two sequences. This causes a String Index Out Of Bounds Exception when the two sequences have different lengths, as `regionMatches` attempts to access characters beyond the end of the shorter sequence. This behavior matches the bug report which states that `equals` fails with a String Index OBE on sequences of different lengths. The failing test confirms this by passing sequences `"abc"` and `"abcd"`, which differ in length. The root cause is that the length passed to `regionMatches` should be the minimum of the two lengths to avoid out-of-bound accesses. Recent bug reports do not relate to this issue, so the focus should be on correcting the length calculation in `StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence)`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
